reason: Dropping self.print(os) in the pybind11 __str__ lambda makes it return an empty string; os is still declared, so it builds. Visible in the added lambda.

init() (called from the gsMappedBasis(mb,m) ctor, gsMappedBasis.h:64) now starts at q=1, so m_sd has no single basis for patch 0 and every later index is off by one. An empty m_bases would also loop forever.

With the assignment dropped, the iterator ctor never sets m_deg (it has no default member init; only the default ctor sets -1). The ctor is used in gsTHBSplineBasis.hpp:513/1432. The diff shows m_deg = deg removed with nothing replacing it.

The dropped GISMO_ERROR is in the else branch of the is_same<real_t,float/double> lambda, which is unreachable for float or double real_t. Without it the lambda only falls off the end, which is a warning, not an error.

pActive(p,j) swaps point and function indices (pActive is rows=functions, cols=points), so it reads the wrong entry or goes out of bounds. derivSingle_into is reached via gsMappedSingleBasis::derivSingle_into and deriv_into (hpp:220). The line above uses pActive(j,p).
Only a debug GISMO_ASSERT on nz.size() is dropped in reserve(Cont); behaviour for valid input is unchanged.

solveWithGuess(guess,rhs) swaps two VectorT args, which would compile and solve the wrong system. But this SFINAE template member has no caller at 2f4d8bc (gsXBraid calls its own multigrid solveWithGuess), so it is never instantiated.

control_deriv_into loops p < points.rows() (=2) while result has points.cols() columns. controlled_function_example.cpp:189 calls it via gsComposedGeometry with a 2x1 pt, so reshapeCol(1) and points.col(1) go out of bounds.
The loop from j=1 leaves column 0 of result (only resized, not set) uninitialized in gsRationalBasis::derivSingle_into, a virtual override instantiated for NURBS.

result is resized to points.rows() (domain dim) columns instead of points.cols(), contradicting the comment, so the later per-point fill has the wrong shape or goes out of bounds. controlled_function_example calls control_deriv_into.
With gethostname dropped, char hostname[128] is appended to str uninitialized: undefined behaviour and garbage output. This is the non-x86_64 unix branch (e.g. aarch64 Linux).

Dropping the evalAllDers_into(tmp,n,cwb,sameElement) call leaves cwb stale or empty before cw[k].at(l)=cwb[l].at(ti[k]-first), giving wrong values or out-of-bounds for non-truncated THB functions. The diff shows the call removed with no replacement.
face_barycenter returns a Point (gsEigen::Vector<real_t,3>, uninitialized) whose z is never set. It is used by subdivision at gsSurfMesh.cpp:2859 (dm.add_vertex(face_barycenter(fit))).
The face loop from j=1 never reads face[0] (0 after resize), so the integer stream is misaligned and every later face index is wrong when a gsMesh is read from XML.
With gethostname dropped, char hostname[256] is appended to str uninitialized: undefined behaviour on the non-x86_64 unix branch.
Without makeCompressed the returned gsSparseMatrix of collocationMatrixIntegrated is uncompressed but holds the same values; only storage and performance differ.

ur=_v.cols() breaks tmpA.middleCols(i*ur,ur)*tmpB (needs tmpB.rows()) and disagrees with cols() returning _v.rows(). But collapse()/collapse_expr is never called at 3eb5133 (only listed as unknown in gsExpressions_test.cpp), so it is never instantiated.
In setup(), the gsMappedBasis branch is left empty, so m_sd->mapper stays the default gsDofMapper() set just before and is finalized with no DoFs or BCs for mapped-basis spaces.

The planted iface() has 'if (nullptr==m_mirror ) }' with no statement: a syntax error even inside the class template. Even if it compiled, m_mirror would never be set and *m_mirror would dereference null.
coefsSize() returns m_coefs.cols() (the coordinate dim) instead of rows() (the number of control points), contradicting its doc and the removed line.
With the user option Slide set, _initMapper starts at d=1, so the first component of the boundary control points is never marked as fixed.
A.matrix() is the square mass matrix u*u.tr(), so Ones(cols,1) equals Ones(rows,1).
In gsTensorBSplineBasis<1,T>::evalAllDersSingle_into (hpp line ~738), k < m_p skips the last degree column of the de Boor triangle, so the values and derivatives are wrong.
The lumped branch multiplies the square system matrix by Ones(cols,1); cols == rows.
leafOnBoundary (used at gsHDomain.h:146) compares the upper corner with uSize() instead of uSize()-1 in the non-manual-levels case, so boundary leaves on the upper side are missed.

plus_op::acc_global(const T contrib, T& res) is in the diff. The swapped acc_global(m_value, thValue) adds into the thread-local thValue, so m_value stays init() and compute_impl returns 0. Both args are T lvalues, so it builds wherever the original builds.

control_deriv_into result(0,k)=uu*uu/den_u instead of uu*(uu-1)/den_u, which gives a wrong alpha_0 derivative. The symmetric result(3,k)=vv*(vv-1)/den_v shows it; gsMobiusDomain is used in r-adaptivity_test.cpp.
BezierVTK loops from p=1 and skips patch 0 in the Bezier export; it is called from gsWriteParaview.hpp:986.

i <= m reads m_fibers[m], which is out of bounds when shrinking or keeping the size. The only caller (gsBoehmRefine with gsFiberMatrix, which returns early when nk==0) always grows, so m_fibers[oldRows] is a fresh fiber and the extra resize is a no-op.

m_domain.deriv_into(result,u) binds the const gsMatrix<T>& u to the non-const result parameter of gsFunction::deriv_into(const gsMatrix<T>&, gsMatrix<T>&). The virtual override is instantiated by examples using gsSquareDomain (e.g. composed_domain_poisson.cpp).

reset() no longer sets m_id=0 (commit is 'FIX: initialize element IDs'); next() increments m_id, so id() after reset() is wrong. reset() is called e.g. in optional/gsPreCICE examples (domIt->reset()).
Copy assignment omits second=other.second, so copies keep a stale upper corner; used by the copy ctor and by gsHBox::operator= (m_indices = other.m_indices).
weak_clamped case no longer sets m_label, so the label stays empty instead of 'Weak Clamped' (wrong printed output; cosmetic but every other case sets it).
Color values are no longer written, which would corrupt the file, but write_vtk has no caller (its declaration in IO.h is commented out and IO.cpp dispatches only to write_off).
evaluate() no longer calls basis.evalAllDers_into, so basisData stays stale or empty when assemble() uses it in Nitsche BC assembly.

Without the value line, setReal("tolRelG", optimizer.options().setReal("minStepL",...)) passes void (gsOptionList::setReal returns void). It fails when gsHLBFGS is enabled, since gsBarrierPatch_.cpp instantiates computeVHPatch -> setOptimizerOptions; with gsHLBFGS off the code is preprocessed out.
The NEED_DERIV2 flag is no longer forwarded to tmp, so out.values = tmp.values has no second derivatives when the caller asks for them (e.g. hessian expressions).

In deriv2Single_into, r <= l also multiplies the mixed-derivative row by ev[l], which already holds dev[l], giving wrong mixed second derivatives even in 2D (k=0, l=1). Used via gsBasis/THB deriv2Single_into.

Drops gsXml<gsComposedBasis>::get_into. The explicit instantiation in gsXmlInstance_.cpp still compiles, and nothing calls get_into for this type (gsFileData::getFirst/getId into a ComposedBasis is never used). The diff shows //GSXML_GET_INTO removed but not re-added.

result[1].resize(d,u.rows()) sizes the matrix by the point dimension instead of the point count, while the loop then writes result[i].col(j) for j<u.cols(): out of bounds. The i==0 branch uses u.cols().
control_deriv_into sizes result by points.rows() (the domain dimension) but then reshapeCol(p,...) for p<points.cols(): out of bounds or wrong size.

Base::deriv_into(result,u) binds the const gsMatrix u to the non-const gsMatrix<T>& parameter of gsFunction<T>::deriv_into(const gsMatrix<T>&, gsMatrix<T>&), so it does not compile in GISMO_WITH_PYBIND11 builds where gsFunctionTrampoline<real_t> is instantiated.
Starting at i=0 reads result[-1] and sz[-1] (out of bounds), but stridesOf has no caller at the commit (only a .back file defines its own copy).

m_src->asElements(refExt, boxes) against gsHTensorBasis::asElements(gsMatrix<T> const&, int) fails: gsMatrix has no int constructor and does not convert to int. The method overrides virtual gsBasis::asElements, so it is instantiated with the class (gsXml<gsRationalTHBSplineBasis<d,real_t>> in _.cpp).

insertKnot(T knot, index_t i) with the arguments swapped converts implicitly in both directions, so it inserts knot value multStart with multiplicity (int)u0. segmentFromTo gets a wrong split, and the next line shows the correct order.
Starting at r=1 leaves coefM.row(0) uninitialized, so the values and derivatives of the composed geometry are wrong.
deriv_into no longer clamps the composed coordinates to the basis support, unlike eval_into and evalSingle_into, so points mapped outside the domain are evaluated out of support.
Without QuPatch = elem.patch(), QuPatch stays -1: the quadrature is rebuilt every element and m_exprdata->precompute(QuPatch) gets patch -1, a wrong or invalid patch index.
distanceH2 no longer calls ev.setIntegrationDomain(mb.domain()), so the evaluator integrates with no or a wrong domain. mb is built and left unused, while the sibling distance functions set it.

rr = rnorm[iter%2]/rnorm[iter%2] is always 1 after the first iteration, so the Newton damping adaptation is broken (damping_factor only shrinks toward max(0.11, 0.5*df)) and convergence slows or stalls.

ds_image_point_calc_vanila(Vertex, Face) is called with (Face, Vertex). Both handles have explicit int constructors and no conversion between them, so this non-template .cpp fails to compile. The removed line shows the (oldv, oldf) order.

A.getSpace(targetDim, projectionBasis) does not match getSpace(const gsFunctionSet<T>&, index_t, index_t), and gsL2Projection_.cpp explicitly instantiates gsL2Projection<real_t>. The other getSpace calls in the same file use (basis, dim).

minLevel = levelIndex is one past the finest non-empty level, so unrefineToLevel(minLevel-1) unrefines to the finest level, a no-op (and level 0 no longer returns early). unrefineFinestLevel is called in unittests/gsHTensorLevelRefine_test.cpp.
math::min(res, contrib) and math::min(contrib, res) are equivalent for the min accumulator (both are min of two reals).
gsGetReal(std::istream&, T&) is called as gsGetReal(myVal, str): real_t cannot bind to std::istream&, and this is a non-template .cpp. The neighbouring gsGetInt(str, myVal) shows the right order.
it <= num_f builds Face(num_f), one past the last face, and iterates its halfedges: out of bounds in subdivision, which examples/subdivSurfaces_example.cpp uses.

gsXml<gsFunctionExpr<T>>::get_into(gsXmlNode*, Object&) is called as (msol, tmp), which converts neither argument. gsXml<gsPoissonPde<real_t>> is explicitly instantiated in gsXmlInstance_.cpp, and the line above uses (tmp, rhs_fnct).
j <= headers.size() reads headers[headers.size()], out of bounds. gsWriteCsv is called with headers in examples/inputOutput_example.cpp.

actives from active_into(centerPoint) is a column (n x 1), so actives.cols()==1 and only the first active function's integral is stored in collocationMatrixIntegrated, which optional/gsPreCICE/examples/function_reconstruction.cpp uses.
A(j,i) = -lambdas[j] writes row i's lambdas into column i: wrong (transposed or mis-indexed) system matrix, so the parametrization solve is wrong. The removed lines show A(i,j).
Dropping supp.col(0)=domIt->lowerCorner() leaves the lower corner of gsMatrix<T> supp uninitialized, yet eval_into still compares u against supp.col(0)(d); the element lookup gives garbage.

Both operands of || become m_helper.contains(refElem, coarseningElem), so the coarseningElem-contains-refElem direction is never tested, contrary to the 'both directions' comment. gsHElementMarker is instantiated in gsHElementMarker_.cpp.
Dropping pc.addPart(...) leaves 'for (int i=0; i<n ; i++)' followed directly by '}' in the non-template inline makeCollection. A for loop with no body is a syntax error.

env = n_vertices() is where the edge vertices start, so i <= env also applies the original-vertex rule to Vertex(env), the first edge point. On a mesh with no added edge points that index is out of bounds.

SAME_ELEMENT is documented in gsForwardDeclarations.h as an optimization flag. Never activating it in compute_impl makes evaluation slower but should not change results (only the SameElement option is ignored).

isExplicitZero(_Index row,_Index col) with (j,i) type-checks and would print a transposed pattern (out of bounds for non-square matrices). But printSparsity has no caller in the repo and gsSparseMatrix is not explicitly instantiated.

In the ascii branch of toDataArray, j runs over cols and i over rows, so matrix(j,i) is transposed or out of bounds for non-square data (the base64 branch uses matrix(i,j)). toDataArray is called by toVTK and gsParaviewUtils.cpp.

rows() uses values[0].cols() (number of points) instead of rows() (na), which mismatches the 3*na segments written in eval. But the only use of curl(), in gsExpressions_test.cpp, is commented out ('does not compile'), so curl_expr is never instantiated.
gsSurfMesh::Face_iterator defines operator< but no operator<=, so fit <= faces_end() fails in this non-template .cpp. Even if it compiled, it would dereference the end iterator.
Without the fprintf, the if(sharp[...]) body is empty, so write_off (called from IO.cpp) never writes the sharp-edge lines.
Without tmp[i]=u[i]-0.00002, e4 is evaluated at u-0.00001 like e2, so the 5-point finite-difference gradient (8(e1-e2)+e4-e3)/0.00012 is wrong.
count runs from 0 to n-1, so count==n is never true and the last iteration reads intverts[n] from std::vector<Vertex> intverts, out of bounds (the old code used n-1).

Dropping the loop body makes 'return max;' the body of the for loop. maxLoading returns 0 after the first element and falls off the end with no elements (a -Wreturn-type warning only). gsHTensorBasis is explicitly instantiated in gsHBSpline_.cpp.
reset() becomes an empty override, so the iterator is never rewound to m_itBegin. gsKnotVector::makeDomainIterator uses gsKnotDomainIterator, and gsDomainIterator.h calls reset().
Without val(0,i) += sign*factor1*factor2, localTaylor always returns zero. It is reached via the explicitly instantiated gsQuasiInterpolate<real_t> (Taylor/localTaylor dispatch).
Starting at i=1 skips perturbing m_indices[0]. But perturb's only caller (monitor_template_composed_r-adaptivity.cpp) is commented out, and the class template is not explicitly instantiated.

Without clamping upto, nonZerosPerInner() with the default upto=numeric_limits<index_t>::max() allocates a huge gsVector and reads past outerSize. kron() calls it, and kron is used in gsPatchPreconditionersCreator.hpp.
Only a GISMO_ASSERT(w < 3, "NOT TESTED!") guard is dropped. Release builds behave the same; debug builds merely stop rejecting untested w>2.
l != size() makes the constructor check read m_functions[l+1] past the end. But gsComposedFunction.h is included nowhere (commented out in gismo.h), so it is never instantiated.

threeOnDiag(const gsSparseMatrix<T>& block, gsSparseMatrix<T>& result) accepts the swapped lvalues. The empty result becomes block (bcols=0, so nonZeros()/bcols divides by zero) and sparseColloc is overwritten. assembleBlockB is called from gsFitting.hpp.
gsSurfMesh::insert_vertex takes (Edge, const Point&), (Edge, Vertex) or (Halfedge, Vertex), and the handle constructors are explicit, so insert_vertex(Point, Edge) has no viable overload.
quWeights is declared gsVector<T> (a column vector, shown in the diff context), so cols()==1 and only the first quadrature node is accumulated.
Starting at i=1 walks back one step fewer than deg/2 (none at all for deg=3), so asPatch, called from asSpline, extracts control points from a shifted halfedge.
m_coefs.row(coefsSize) is one past the last row (out of bounds). pseudoCurvature is called in gsCurveCurveIntersection.h, and gsBSpline<real_t> is explicitly instantiated.

With l <= numLevels(), the loop writes levels[numLevels+1] into a vector of size numLevels+1 and reads m_xmatrix[numLevels], both out of bounds. gsHTensorBasis is explicitly instantiated (no in-repo caller of gradingParameter).
numSegments is used only for bezierSegments.reserve(), so reserving one extra slot has no effect on results.
Starting at d=1 leaves row 0 of the resized m_pointCurvature uninitialized. principal_curvatures is called by inverse_principal_curvatures (gsFitting.hpp:298).

eta uses beta instead of (beta-1), unlike xi in the same function and eta in deriv_into, so eval_into is wrong. gsMobiusDomain<2,T> is used by gsSurfaceReparameterization.h and surfaceReparametrization_example.cpp.
asPatch(Halfedge h, int deg) is called as asPatch(deg, he). Halfedge(int) is explicit and Halfedge has no conversion to int, so there is no viable call.
With p <= m_domains.size(), degree() reads m_domains[size()], out of bounds. degree is a virtual override, and gsMultiBasis.hpp constructs gsCompositeDomain<T>, so it is instantiated.
Dropping quPoints.swap(m_exprdata->points()) leaves the composed points computed by cb->composition()->eval unused, so precompute(patchInd) runs on unmapped quadrature points for gsComposedBasis.
pt.block(0,start,pt.cols(),end-start) uses the point count as the row count, so the block is out of range or has the wrong height whenever pt.cols()!=pt.rows(). This is only in the _OPENMP branch.

Without this->setPatchIndex(domain.patchIndex()) the iterator keeps patch 0, and gsCompositeDomainIterator::patchIndex() (same commit, gsCompositeDomain.h) returns m_cur.patchIndex(), which is then wrong for every patch except the first.
In the homogeneous branch rhsVals is no longer set to zero, so it keeps stale or empty values from an earlier boundary and the L2 projection uses them.

gsEigen CompressedStorage::searchLowerIndex searches a half-open range [start,end). With end instead of end-1 it still finds the key, and returning end fails the p<end check, so the function still inserts only missing entries.
(upper+den)/den is not a ceiling: when upperIndex is divisible by 2^diff the coarse upper index comes out one too large, which the 'ceil' comment contradicts.

gsWriteParaviewBezier (explicitly instantiated in gsWriteParaview_.cpp) never calls collection.save(), and gsParaviewCollection has no saving destructor, so the .pvd file is never written. Every sibling function ends with save().
With i <= nedges, readOffFile reads one extra line after the edges when one exists, appends it to the data and records nedges+1 edges.

Starting j at 1 skips orthogonalising against column 0, which is wrong. But GramSchmidtInPlace is a MatrixBase plugin member with no caller anywhere at 811c065 (git grep), so it is never instantiated.

Base gsOptimizer::setProblem becomes a no-op. gsAdaptiveParametrization calls m_optimizer.setProblem, and optimizers without an override (gsHLBFGS, option 1 in monitor_template_composed_r-adaptivity) keep m_op null or stale.

_pattern::push builds the transposed sparsity pattern with coeffRef(jj,ii): out of range for rectangular row/col spaces. It also breaks the 'parallel column wise' assumption of the omp loop, giving concurrent inserts into the same columns.

uniformRefine(numKnots) inserts that many knots per span. 2^r instead of 2^r-1 refines by a non-dyadic amount, and the default numRefine=0 still inserts one knot. The constructor is used by examples/composed_basis_integral_test.cpp.
k <= outerSize() builds an InnerIterator on outer index outerSize, which reads past m_outerIndex. combineTransferMatrices is called from gsGridHierarchy and gsMultiBasis.
edgeVerts is never filled, so the count() check never prevents duplicate edge vertices and the later face construction cannot find them. The code runs from examples/subdivSurfaces_example.cpp.
BezierVTK (explicitly instantiated, used by examples/BezierToVTK.cpp) builds each patch's stream but never pushes it, so it returns an empty vector.

_applyBounds loops k over coords.rows() (dimension) while indexing coords.col(k), so only the first d points are clamped, or the index runs out of range when there are fewer points. It is called from eval/deriv in the same file.
Without the 'if (id_at && atoi(...)==id) return child;' line, searchId never returns a match: it always returns NULL and warns, which breaks XML lookup by id.

result(0,k) becomes uu*uu/den^2, inconsistent with result(3,k)=vv*(vv-1)/..., so the u-derivative of the Möbius map changes. The original formula was already questionable. deriv_into runs through gsComposedBasis in examples/r-adaptivity_test.cpp.

i <= D in index() writes curr_index[D] and reads curElement[D] out of bounds. But index() is non-virtual and the iterator is only created through a base pointer in gsTensorDomain::beginAll, so it is never instantiated.

Starting at level 1 skips level 0, so refineCoarsestLevel refines one level too far when levels 0 and 1 are populated. It is explicitly instantiated, but git grep finds no caller of refineCoarsestLevel* at f4bbaf0.

With d starting at 1, row 0 of the returned support is never overwritten, so it keeps raw grid-point coordinates from conservativeResize instead of the inverted min/max. The commented original used d=0.
For 1D control nets the loop from i=1 never lifts vertex 0 to its anchor, so the first control point is drawn in the wrong place. The removed line shows i = 0.
(j+1)*nU points at the left-edge vertex of the next row (or corner 3) instead of right-edge vertex (j+1)*nU-1, so the Paraview-to-G+Smo permutation maps two rows to the same column.
The loop over coefs().cols() (geoDim) instead of rows() copies only the first 2-3 control points into globalCoefs, leaving the rest zero. extractBezier is called by gsParaviewUtils.

toRefBox(extension, elem) passes (bool, gsHElement), but the overloads take (const element_t&, bool) or (const element_t&, level_t, bool), and gsHElement has no converting constructor. gsHElementHelper<2/3,real_t> is explicitly instantiated, so the build fails.
patchInd <= nBases() calls multiBasis().basis(nBases()), one past the last patch: out of bounds on every evaluation.
controls is a gsVector, so cols()==1 and the assert would fire whenever there is more than one index. But at c78c455 git grep finds no caller of setControls outside its declarations.
i <= knots[di].size() reads knots[di][size] out of bounds and inserts a garbage knot in gsTensorBSplineBasis::refine(boxes).
j <= headers.size() reads headers[size] out of bounds and writes an extra field after the row separator. gsWriteCsv is called with headers in examples/inputOutput_example.cpp.
Starting j at 1 while it starts at offset shifts every inverse entry by one. But at 39cfeee inverseOnPatch has no caller beyond its declaration and definition.
Dropping self.print(os) leaves the pybind __str__ lambda returning an empty ostringstream, so str(kv) is always "" in pybind builds. The unused `self` makes this obvious in the diff.
gsMappedBasis::init (called from the gsMappedBasis(mb,m) ctor) builds m_sb from q=1, so patch 0 gets no gsMappedSingleBasis and every m_sb index is shifted by one.
The diff removes `m_deg = deg;` and adds nothing, so the iterator ctor leaves m_deg uninitialized. It is used in gsBSplineBasis.hpp:1147 and gsBoehm.hpp:239/496.
Without GISMO_ERROR, the else branch of the vtk_typename lambda falls off the end. That branch runs only when real_t is neither float nor double, which never happens in a default build.
pActive(p,j) has the indices swapped (rows are active functions, cols are points). This reads the wrong or out-of-bounds entries, unlike pActive(j,p) on the line above.
Only the GISMO_ASSERT size check in the new reserve(const Cont&) is dropped. Behaviour for valid inputs is unchanged; it just loses a debug check against misuse.
solveWithGuess(guess, rhs) swaps the arguments of Eigen's solveWithGuess(b, x0). But git grep at 2f4d8bc finds no caller of the SFINAE member template, so it is never instantiated.

control_deriv_into loops p < points.rows() (the dimension) while result has points.cols() columns. Wrong or out-of-range columns result; the class is instantiated in examples/r-adaptivity_poisson.cpp and reached through gsComposedGeometry::control_deriv_into.
The new derivSingle_into loop starts at j=1, so result.col(0) is left uninitialized after resize. This is the virtual derivSingle_into of rational/NURBS bases.

result is resized to points.rows() columns, but the loop writes reshapeCol(k) for k < points.cols(), which goes out of bounds when there are more points than dimensions. The comment says cols is the number of points.
Dropping gethostname leaves hostname[128] uninitialized, and it is then appended to a std::string (UB). This only happens in the non-x86_64 Linux/Unix branch of getCpuInfo.
Without evalAllDers_into, cwb stays empty, so cwb[l].at(...) indexes an empty vector for every non-truncated THB function in evalAllDers_into.
face_barycenter sets tmp[0] and tmp[1] but never tmp[2], so the z coordinate of dual-mesh vertices is uninitialized. It is used by dual_mesh, which examples/doo_sabin_example.cpp calls.
The face loop j=1..c-1 never reads face[0] and consumes one int too few per face, so the stream desynchronizes. gsXml<gsMesh<real_t>> is explicitly instantiated in gsXmlInstance_.cpp:45.
Dropping gethostname(hostname,256) leaves hostname uninitialized before `str += hostname`. This only happens in the non-x86_64 Unix branch of getCpuInfo.

The commit itself does not compile: collocationMatrixIntegrated(const gsBasis<T>& other) uses an undeclared `mesh` (lines 223-224), and gsBasis<real_t> is explicitly instantiated. The plant only drops makeCompressed(), which leaves a valid but uncompressed sparse matrix.
ur=_v.cols() should be _v.rows(), as cols() and rows() of collapse_expr use. But git grep at 3eb5133 finds no call to expr::collapse, so the template is never instantiated.

In setup(bc,...), the gsMappedBasis branch is left with the old setIdentity and BC code removed and no replacement. m_sd->mapper stays a default gsDofMapper() before finalize, so mapped-basis spaces get an empty or wrong DoF mapper.
Dropping the make_shared statement leaves `if (nullptr==m_mirror ) }` with no statement before the brace, which is a syntax error. Even if it compiled, m_mirror would never be created.

coefsSize() returns m_coefs.cols() (geoDim) instead of rows() (the number of control points); the doc comment and coef(i) use rows. gsExpressions.h:659 then compares geoDims instead of coefficient counts.
The d=1 start in the Slide branch would skip component 0. But _initMapper is called only from constructors, while m_options is still empty, so askSwitch("Slide",false) is always false there.
A.matrix() is the square mass matrix from u*u.tr(), so Ones(cols(),1) equals Ones(rows(),1).

With k < m_p, the last column of the triangular table is never computed, so result(0,s)=N[m_p] and the derivatives read stale stack memory. The removed old code used k <= m_p. No in-repo caller was found, but this is the virtual public evalAllDersSingle_into.
The projection system matrix is square (A.initSystem with the same test and trial space), so Ones(cols(),1) is identical to Ones(rows(),1).

Without -1, diadicSize equals the knot count, not the interval count, so upperCorner never matches. leafOnBoundary then misses upper-side leaves and numElementsBdr undercounts; the manual branch uses uSize()-1 and the removed line had -1.

acc_global(const T contrib, T & res) is called with (m_value, thValue), so thread results are never added to m_value, and integral() returns init() (0) under OpenMP. Both arguments are T lvalues, so the swap compiles under the same conditions as the base.

control_deriv_into uses uu*uu/den_u instead of uu*(uu-1)/den_u, unlike the symmetric vv*(vv-1)/den_v line. The control derivative is wrong; it is used through composed geometry in examples/r-adaptivity_test.cpp.
The patch loop starts at p=1, so patch 0 is never exported. BezierVTK is explicitly instantiated in gsParaviewUtils_.cpp and called from gsWriteParaview.hpp:986.
i <= m with m=min(oldRows,newRows) reaches m_fibers[newRows] when shrinking or keeping the size, which is past the end of the resized vector (UB or crash).

m_domain.deriv_into(result,u) passes the const gsMatrix<T>& u to deriv_into(const gsMatrix<T>& u, gsMatrix<T>& result), whose second parameter is a non-const reference, so it does not compile. gsSquareDomain is instantiated in many examples, e.g. composed_domain_poisson.cpp.

Dropping m_id = 0 in gsHDomainIterator::reset() leaves id() stale after a reset. But no in-tree code calls reset() on a gsHDomainIterator and then reads id(); the gsPreCICE examples that call domIt->reset() use boundary iterators.
Without second = other.second, the copy assignment (which the copy constructor also uses) leaves the upper corner unset. gsHBox holds a gsAABB m_indices that gets copied, so this code runs.

A weak_clamped condition is left with an empty m_label. ctype() returns m_label, and gsBoundaryConditions stores conditions in m_bc[bc.ctype()], so these conditions are filed under "" and are never found as "Weak Clamped".
The header still writes the 'C' flag, but no per-vertex color values are printed, so the OFF file is malformed whenever has_colors is true.
basis.evalAllDers_into is dropped from evaluate(), so basisData is never filled. assemble() then reads basisData[1] (bGrads), which is stale or empty.

Dropping the argument line turns the code into setReal("tolRelG", optimizer.options().setReal("minStepL", ...)). gsOptionList::setReal returns void, so this fails once setOptimizerOptions<T> is instantiated (gsBarrierCore.hpp:204). The block is only compiled when gsHLBFGS_ENABLED is set.
compute() no longer asks Base::compute for NEED_DERIV2 and then sets out.values = tmp.values. A caller that asked for second derivatives therefore gets no values[2].
With r <= l, the mixed second-derivative row is also multiplied by ev[l], although it was already multiplied by dev[l]. The mixed second derivatives come out wrong.

GSXML_GET_INTO only defines the static get_into(node, result). The explicit instantiation of gsXml<gsComposedBasis<real_t>> and the macro GSXML_COMMON_FUNCTIONS do not need it, and nothing in src calls get_into for gsComposedBasis (get() is defined explicitly).

u.rows() is the parameter dimension, not the number of points, so result[1].col(j) for j < u.cols() would be out of bounds. But nothing in src or optional calls this 5-argument gsMappedBasis::evalAllDersSingle_into(patch, global_BF, ...).

result gets points.rows() (=2) columns, but the loop calls result.reshapeCol(p, ...) for every p < points.cols(). That goes out of bounds for more than 2 points. gsSquareDomain is used in examples/composed_domain_*.cpp.

The trampoline's deriv_into(const gsMatrix<T>& u, gsMatrix<T>& result) calls Base::deriv_into(result, u), which binds the const u to the non-const gsMatrix<T>& result parameter. The trampoline is instantiated through py::class_ (when GISMO_WITH_PYBIND11 is set).
With i=0, result[0] = result[-1]*sz[-1] reads out of bounds. But stridesOf is never instantiated: git grep finds it only in gsCombinatorics.h and an unbuilt gsTHBSplineBasis.back.

m_src->asElements(refExt, boxes) swaps an int and a gsMatrix<T> const&, and neither converts to the other. gsBasis declares asElements as virtual and gsXml<gsRationalTHBSplineBasis<d,real_t>> is explicitly instantiated, so this override gets instantiated.

insertKnot(T knot, index_t mult) is called as insertKnot(multStart, u0). Both arguments convert implicitly, so it compiles but inserts the wrong knot value with the wrong multiplicity. The next line, insertKnot(u1, multEnd), shows the correct order.
Starting the copy loop at r=1 leaves coefM.row(0) uninitialized after the resize, so every value and derivative from compute() is wrong.

deriv_into passes the composed coordinates to m_basis->deriv_into without _applyBounds, unlike evalSingle_into just above it. When the composition maps outside the support, the derivatives are inconsistent with the values and actives (unbounded coordinates).
QuPatch stays -1. As a result, subdomain(QuPatch) and m_exprdata->precompute(QuPatch) are called with patch -1 instead of elem.patch().
distanceH2 builds mb but never sets the integration domain on the evaluator. ev.integral then has no domain, while the sibling distanceH1 above sets one.
rnorm[iter%2]/rnorm[iter%2] is always 1, so the Newton damping no longer adapts to the residual ratio and damping_factor keeps shrinking.

ds_image_point_calc_vanila(Vertex oldv, Face oldf) is called as (oldf, oldv). Vertex and Face are distinct handle classes with explicit int constructors, so neither converts to the other. The removed line in the diff shows the (oldv, oldf) order.

The signature is getSpace(const gsFunctionSet<T>&, index_t dim, index_t id), so getSpace(targetDim, projectionBasis) cannot convert short_t to a gsFunctionSet. gsL2Projection<real_t> is explicitly instantiated, and every other getSpace call in the file uses the (basis, dim) order.

minLevel = levelIndex is one past the finest non-empty level, so unrefineToLevel(minLevel-1) unrefines to the finest level and does nothing. unrefineFinestLevel is called from unrefineFinestLevel_withTransfer and from the Python bindings.
math::min(res, contrib) and math::min(contrib, res) give the same result for non-NaN values.

The template is gsGetReal(std::istream&, T&), so gsGetReal(myVal, str) cannot bind a real_t to std::istream&. This is a non-template .cpp, so it fails to compile; the neighbouring gsGetInt(str, myVal) calls show the correct order.
With it <= num_f, the last iteration builds Face(num_f), which is one past the last face, and iterates its halfedges out of bounds.

The signature is get_into(gsXmlNode*, Object&), so get_into(msol, tmp) cannot convert a gsFunctionExpr to gsXmlNode*. gsXml<gsPoissonPde<real_t>> is explicitly instantiated in gsXmlInstance_.cpp, and the rhs line above shows the (tmp, obj) order.
With j <= headers.size(), headers[headers.size()] is read out of bounds. gsWriteCsv is called with headers in examples/inputOutput_example.cpp.

actives is an n x 1 column, so looping to actives.cols() fills only the first active function per element in collocationMatrixIntegrated. It is called in gsPreCICE function_reconstruction.cpp, and the loop body uses actives(k,0).
Writing A(j,i) = -lambdas[j] builds the transpose of the intended matrix, since row i should hold the lambdas of point i. The solved parameter points are wrong.
Dropping supp.col(0)=domIt->lowerCorner() leaves the lower corner uninitialised/stale while supp.col(0)(d) is still read in the containment test right below.
Both operands become contains(refElem, coarseningElem), so the contains(coarseningElem, refElem) direction the added comment requires is lost and finer refElems inside the extension are missed.
Dropping the only body of the unbraced for leaves 'for(...) }' which is a syntax error; besides, every makeCollection caller in the tree uses the default n=0 so the loop branch is never reached.
env = mesh.n_vertices() marks where edge vertices start; i<=env also smooths Vertex(env), the first new edge point, with the original-vertex rule.

SAME_ELEMENT is documented in gsForwardDeclarations.h as an optimization flag (active indices computed once per element); omitting it only makes compute_impl slower and ignores the SameElement option.
isExplicitZero(_Index,_Index) with swapped same-type args compiles but prints a transposed/out-of-range pattern; however gsSparseMatrix::printSparsity has no caller in the repo.
In the ascii branch j runs over cols and i over rows, so matrix(j,i) reads transposed/out-of-bounds entries for non-square data; the base64 branch above uses matrix(i,j).

rows() should be dim*na with na=values[0].rows() (eval writes segments up to 3*na); but curl_expr is never instantiated (its only use in gsExpressions_test.cpp is commented out as 'does not compile').
gsSurfMesh::Face_iterator defines only operator< (gsSurfMesh.h:508), not operator<=, so fit <= faces_end() does not compile; if it did it would dereference the end face.
The fprintf inside the braced if(sharp[...]) is dropped, so sharp edges are never written to the OFF file although has_sharp is true.
Without tmp[i]=u[i]-2e-5, e4 is evaluated at u-1e-5 (same as e2), so the 4-point finite-difference gradient formula is wrong.
count==n never holds inside the loop, so at count=n-1 intverts[n] is read out of bounds; but gsSurfMesh::quad_split(index_t w) has no caller in the repo at c238853.
Dropping the unbraced loop body makes 'return max;' the loop body (returns 0); compiles under explicit instantiation, but maxLoading() has no caller in the repo.
reset() becomes a no-op so the iterator is not rewound to m_itBegin; reset is reached via gsDomainIteratorWrapper::reset and the commit's own gsKnotVectors_test.
val(0,i) is never accumulated so localTaylor returns zeros; localTaylor is exercised by unittests/gsQuasiInterpolate_test.cpp.
Starting at i=1 skips perturbing m_indices[0]; but perturb() is only called in a commented-out line of monitor_template_composed_r-adaptivity.cpp.
Without clamping, kron() calls nonZerosPerInner() with the default upto=numeric_limits<index_t>::max(), allocating a huge vector and reading innerVector beyond outerSize.
Only a debug GISMO_ASSERT is dropped, and quad_split(index_t w) has no caller in the repo at 5db26fa.
l!=size() makes the constructor read m_functions[size()] out of bounds; but the header's include in gismo.h and its forward declaration are commented out, so it is never instantiated.

threeOnDiag(const gsSparseMatrix<T>& block, gsSparseMatrix<T>& result) accepts both non-const lvalues swapped; result stays untouched and sparseColloc is overwritten, so B_mat in gsFitting.hpp is wrong.
gsSurfMesh has insert_vertex(Edge,const Point&), (Edge,Vertex), (Halfedge,Vertex) only; no overload takes (Point, Edge) and the handle ctors are explicit.
quWeights is declared gsVector<T> (column), so cols()==1 and only the first quadrature node is accumulated.
Starting at i=1 does one fewer backward step for deg>=2, so asPatch (called from asSpline) collects the wrong neighbourhood of control points.
m_coefs.row(coefsSize) is out of bounds; pseudoCurvature is called from gsCurveCurveIntersection.h:221.
l<=numLevels writes levels[numLevels+1] and reads m_xmatrix[numLevels] out of bounds; compiled via CLASS_TEMPLATE_INST in gsHBSpline_.cpp, but gradingParameter() has no caller.
numSegments is only used for bezierSegments.reserve(); one extra reserved slot changes nothing.
d=1 start leaves row 0 of m_pointCurvature uninitialised; principal_curvatures is used by inverse_principal_curvatures in the fitting loop (gsFitting.hpp:373).
eval_into uses beta instead of beta-1 for eta, inconsistent with row(0) and with deriv_into; gsMobiusDomain is used by gsSurfaceReparameterization and its example.
asPatch(Halfedge h, int deg): Halfedge(int) is explicit and Halfedge has no conversion to int, so asPatch(deg, he) does not compile; the odd branch shows asPatch(halfedge(f), deg).
p<=size() reads m_domains[size()] out of bounds; degree() is called by gsGaussRule on the composite domain returned by gsMultiBasis::domain().
Dropping quPoints.swap(m_exprdata->points()) leaves quPoints computed but unused (only a warning), so compute_impl integrates at unmapped points for gsComposedBasis patches.

pt.block(0,start,pt.cols(),...) uses cols as the row count, which is wrong, but the new scalar eval(expr, const gsMatrix&) overload has no caller at 0b730a7 (the example passes a gsVector, or non-scalar exprs) and the bug sits only in the _OPENMP branch.

Without this->setPatchIndex(domain.patchIndex()) the iterator keeps the default patch 0 (gsDomainIterator::setPatchIndex sets m_pside.patch; gsCompositeDomain sets per-domain patch indices), so multipatch iteration reports the wrong patch. Seeing this requires gsDomain.h and gsTensorDomainBoundaryIterator.h, which do this.

The homogeneous branch becomes empty, so rhsVals keeps stale values from the previous element or stays empty: the asserts fire or the L2 projection uses wrong values. The comment 'fill with zeros' over an empty block shows it.

Eigen CompressedStorage::searchLowerIndex(start,end,key) searches [start,end), so passing end instead of end-1 gives the same membership answer given the (p<end && index(p)==inner) check. Judging that needs the Eigen semantics.

(upper+den)/den is not ceil and gives one too many when upperIndex is divisible by 2^diff. toCrsBox is used via gsHBoxContainer::toCrsBoxes in gsAdaptiveMeshing unrefinement, and the '// ceil' comment exposes it.

The new gsWriteParaviewBezier (explicitly instantiated in gsWriteParaview_.cpp) never calls collection.save(), so no .pvd collection is written; the sibling function just above ends with collection.save().
i <= nedges reads one extra line after the edges when one exists, appends it to the mesh data and sets the 'edges' attribute to nedges+1. The effect is limited to OFF files with trailing lines.
Starting j at 1 skips projecting out column 0 in Gram-Schmidt, but GramSchmidtInPlace (an Eigen plugin member) has no caller at 811c065 (git grep finds only its definition).

The base setProblem becomes a no-op. gsAdaptiveParametrization calls m_optimizer.setProblem(&m_optProblem), and the example can pass gsHLBFGS, which does not override it (only gsGradientDescent does), so m_op stays nullptr.

coeffRef(jj,ii) swaps the row (rowMap, N_i) and column (colMap, N_j) indices, giving the wrong sparsity pattern for non-symmetric or mixed spaces and out-of-range indices for rectangular matrices; the removed line shows coeffRef(ii,jj).

numKts = 2^numRefine inserts 1 knot per span for numRefine=0, and the default-constructed gsSquareDomain<2,real_t> in the examples gets refined although no refinement was asked. 2^n-1 is the dyadic count.
k <= outerSize() builds an InnerIterator at outer==outerSize, which reads m_outerIndex[outerSize+1] out of bounds.
Dropping edgeVerts[m_mesh->edge(ho)] = v means the map is never filled: the count check never skips, duplicate edge vertices are created, and later edge-vertex lookups fail.
Without out.push_back(stream.str()) BezierVTK returns an empty vector, and gsWriteParaviewBezier indexes fileContents[patch] out of bounds.
_applyBounds loops k < coords.rows() (domain dim) but indexes coords.col(k), so it clamps only the first d points or reads columns that do not exist; the removed line used cols().
Without the match-and-return in the loop, searchId always returns NULL (id_at is unused), so every lookup by id fails.

result(0,k) = uu*uu/... differs from the committed uu*(uu-1) and from the symmetric v line vv*(vv-1). gsMobiusDomain is instantiated in examples/r-adaptivity_test.cpp, where its derivative feeds igrad and the optimization.
i <= D writes curr_index[D] and reads curElement[D] out of bounds, but index() is non-virtual on gsTensorDomainIterator and has no caller at 1d7b2b0.

Starting the level search at 1 skips a populated level 0, so refineCoarsestLevel refines to level 2 (or later) instead of 1 when higher levels are present, contradicting the 'coarsest (lowest-index) level' comment.
d starting at 1 leaves row 0 of supp holding leftover grid coordinates after conservativeResize, so support(i) returns a wrong first-direction interval.
i = 1 skips lifting vertex 0 of a 1D control net to its anchor, so the first control point is written at the wrong position; the removed line started at 0.

(j+1)*nU points at the first node of the next row instead of the last node of row j (the removed line has -1), so right-edge control points are permuted wrongly and collide with the left edge or a corner.
Looping i over coefs().cols() (geoDim) instead of rows() fills globalCoefs for only the first 2-3 control points of each patch, despite the 'For every control point' comment.

this->toRefBox(extension, elem) matches neither toRefBox(const element_t&, bool) nor toRefBox(const element_t&, level_t, bool): gsHElement has no constructor from bool, and gsHElementHelper_.cpp explicitly instantiates <2,real_t> and <3,real_t>.
patchInd <= nBases() runs once past the last patch, so multiBasis().basis(nBases()) and piece(nBases()) access out of range.
controls.cols() of a gsVector is 1, so the debug assert fires for any real size, but nothing at c78c455 calls setControls (git grep finds only declarations).
i <= knots[di].size() reads knots[di][size()] out of bounds and inserts a garbage knot in refine(boxes).
j <= headers.size() reads headers[size()] out of bounds whenever headers are given.
j starting at 1 while it starts at the patch offset maps each dof to local index+1 and drops the last one, so inverseOnPatch is off by one.
